description: Steady B2 content batch for The Sound Maze. Each target is spoken aloud; the learner selects its spelling. Draft content is not wired into the live game.

questions.explain: Frantic has /æ/ in its first stressed syllable. Frontier has /ʌ/ or /ɔ/ depending on pronunciation and a different syllable pattern; the other forms are not standard words.
Subtle has /ʌ/ in its first syllable. Settle has /ɛ/, saddle has /æ/, and soothe has /uː/.
Reckless has /ɛ/ in its first syllable. The other options are not standard spellings of this word.
Mnemonic begins with /n/ because the initial m is silent. Pneumatic begins with /n/ too, while magnetic begins with /m/ and phonetic with /f/.
Xenon begins with /z/, the usual sound of initial x in this word. Senate and cenotaph begin with /s/, while zenith begins with /z/ but has a different vowel and ending.
Psalm begins with /s/ because the p is silent. Salmon begins with /s/ too but has a different ending; palm begins with /p/ in many General American pronunciations, and qualm begins with /kw/.
Promptly ends with /tli/. Prompt ends with /t/, prompts with /ts/, and prompter with /tər/.
Twelfth ends with /lfθ/. Twelve ends with /lv/, and twelfths adds a final /s/; twelfthly is not a standard common word.
Risked ends with /t/ because -ed follows the voiceless /k/ sound. Risks ends with /s/, risky with /i/, and risen with /ən/.
Liaison is spelled l-i-a-i-s-o-n. The other options omit or rearrange letters.
Supersede ends with -sede, not -cede or -ceed. The spelling is unusual and often confused.
Occurrence has double c and double r, and it ends with -ence. The other choices omit or change letters.
